1) Controller/Processor: Acme expects Redwood to be the processor handling ACME customer data for inference. Please confirm the DPA language explicitly states Redwood acts as Processor and ACME remains Controller.

2) Subprocessors: we need a current list of subprocessors and an agreement to notify us of changes 30 days before onboarding any new subprocessor.

4) Data Residency / Logs: For compliance we need logs and any persisted request/response data to be stored in the US (preferably us-east-1). Also want to confirm default retention for request logs and options to shorten retention (PII minimization).

5) PII Handling: we need to know whether Redwood stores raw inference inputs and outputs by default and whether redaction/tokenization is available as an option (and if so, how that impacts model quality).

If you can provide short, technical answers to the bullets above and the subprocessors link, we can flag anything urgent in our redlines. If helpful, we can schedule another 30-min session with Legal + Security.

Hi all — following up with the technical answers for ACME's questions below. Short version up top, details after.

Summary answers:
- Controller/Processor: Redwood operates as a Processor for inference requests; DPA language should reflect that (we can provide exact clause suggestions).
- Subprocessors: current subprocessors list: AWS (infrastructure), S3 backups (Amazon S3), Datadog (monitoring), Fastly (CDN). We publish an up-to-date list at https://redwood.com/subprocessors and we notify affected customers via email 30 days prior to onboarding a new subprocessor.
- Breach Notice: Redwood's standard practice is to notify customers within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that impacts customer data. We can include that in the DPA.
- Data Residency / Logs: Primary production inference logs are stored in AWS us-east-1 by default. Customers on Private/Dedicated can choose region; hosted customers may request region constraints (subject to capacity).
- Retention & PII: Default retention for request/response logs is 30 days (used for debugging, quality/regression monitoring). We offer configurable retention down to 0 days (no persistence) for an additional configuration; we also offer automated redaction/tokenization options at the SDK/proxy layer to prevent raw PII from being persisted.
- Encryption & Access: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest (AES-256). Access to logs is restricted via RBAC; audit logs capture admin access.

Details / notes:
- Raw inputs/outputs: by default we persist request metadata and a short-lived cached KV for latency optimization. Full raw payloads are persisted under default retention (30 days) unless the customer enables "no persistence" or redaction option. We'll document the quality tradeoffs for redaction (some prompts may degrade accuracy depending on what is removed).
- Subprocessor link and docs: https://redwood.com/subprocessors (this page includes contact & notification process).
- DPA clause: suggested wording — "Redwood Inference acts as Processor on behalf of Customer, processing Customer Data per Controller instructions as set forth in the DPA". Legal can refine but that's the canonical position.

Attachments: included a short tech note (attached in thread) summarizing retention config options and a diagram matching the data-flow image Marissa attached.

If helpful, I can join a short call with Acme Security to walk through the options and show where retention/redaction are configured.
